Enqueuing then raises, and submit() marks those failed submissions complete, allowing offsets to advance without processing their results. If a worker stalls or ingestion exceeds processing capacity, the consumer continues reading Kafka and retaining every queued payload. A stalled early offset also keeps later completed offsets in OffsetTracker indefinitely. This can exhaust consumer memory rather than merely backlog Kafka. Consequently, graceful join can return with accepted messages unprocessed, and results completed during worker shutdown are never committed. A normal shutdown or rebalance therefore unnecessarily replays successfully handled results. Stop accepting submissions first, drain accepted work in join(), and flush the final committable offsets afterward."

findings.title: Do not reuse a shut-down queue pool after a rebalance
findings.body: Every strategy created by this factory shares self.queue_pool, but SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close() shuts that pool down. Arroyo closes and recreates processing strategies during partition rebalances, so the replacement strategy receives exited workers and shut-down queues. Enqueuing then raises, and submit() marks those failed submissions complete, allowing offsets to advance without processing their results. Create a fresh pool and offset tracker for each strategy, or implement a safe lifecycle that keeps the shared pool usable across strategy replacements.

findings.title: Do not mark failed processing as completed
findings.body: complete_offset() runs in finally even when result_processor raises. If processing offset 100 fails and offset 101 succeeds, both become committable and the factory commits Kafka offset 102, permanently skipping the failed result without retrying it or sending it to a DLQ. Failed processing must remain outstanding until an explicit recovery or discard policy handles it. The new error-handling test misses this because it checks before the one-second commit loop runs.

findings.title: Bound outstanding work and apply backpressure
findings.body: queue.Queue() is unbounded by default, and submit() always accepts messages without signalling backpressure to Arroyo. If a worker stalls or ingestion exceeds processing capacity, the consumer continues reading Kafka and retaining every queued payload. A stalled early offset also keeps later completed offsets in OffsetTracker indefinitely. This can exhaust consumer memory rather than merely backlog Kafka. Add a finite total in-flight limit and reject submissions when that limit is reached.

findings.title: Drain accepted work and flush offsets during graceful shutdown
findings.body: close() stops and joins the commit thread before workers finish. It then calls pool.shutdown(), which sets worker.shutdown=True, causing workers to exit after their current item rather than drain queued work despite shutdown(immediate=False). Consequently, graceful join can return with accepted messages unprocessed, and results completed during worker shutdown are never committed. A normal shutdown or rebalance therefore unnecessarily replays successfully handled results. Stop accepting submissions first, drain accepted work in join(), and flush the final committable offsets afterward.

findings.title: Honor the processing strategy's join timeout
findings.body: join(timeout) ignores its timeout and calls close(), which waits up to five seconds for each worker separately. With the default twenty queues and stalled handlers, worker joins alone can take about 100 seconds even for join(timeout=0). close() also performs these blocking waits before Arroyo can apply its configured join timeout. This defeats the shutdown/rebalance deadline. Keep close() non-blocking and enforce one shared deadline across worker joins.

findings.title: Reject negative worker counts before starting consumption
findings.body: The CLI accepts any integer for --max-workers, so --max-workers=-1 reaches FixedQueuePool as num_queues=-1. range(-1) creates no queues or workers, and every submission subsequently raises IndexError. SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy catches that error and marks the message complete, so offsets are committed while all results are discarded. Validate that the configured queue count is positive before creating the pool.

findings.title: Synchronize workers before asserting a nonempty queue
findings.body: The worker threads are already running and the test processor returns immediately. All ten items can legitimately be consumed before get_stats() executes, making total_items zero and failing this assertion even though the implementation behaved correctly. Hold the processors behind an event while checking queue depth, then release them to verify completion.

findings.title: Do not require randomized hashes to populate every queue
findings.body: Python string hashes are randomized between interpreter runs. Hashing twenty fixed group keys modulo three does not guarantee that all three queue indices occur; a valid hash seed can place every key in only two queues and fail this test. Verify distribution with controlled hashing or explicitly selected keys instead of asserting full coverage from a probabilistic sample.
